newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army sergeant enters sexual misconduct pleas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army sergeant enters sexual misconduct pleas.

text.p: An Army sergeant who testified in an earlier case that male drill instructors at the Aberdeen Proving Ground carried on a sex "game" with female recruits pleaded guilty Monday to sexual misconduct.

Staff Sgt. Wayne Gamble, a former drill instructor at the base's Ordnance Centre and School, pleaded guilty under an arrangement with military prosecutors to one count of sodomy, nine counts of adultery and 11 counts of fraternisation with recruits at the school, a base spokesman said.

Spokesman John Yaquiant said Gamble also pleaded guilty to going absent without leave -- a charge that was reduced from desertion. Gamble was to be sentenced by a military judge later Monday or Tuesday. He faced a maximum term of 36 years confinement.

Charges against Gamble were dropped pertaining to one count of assault, one count of committing indecent acts, and additional counts of adultery, sodomy, use of indecent language and violating school regulations, Yaquiant said.
In May, Gamble testified against Staff Sgt. Vernell Robinson, a drill instructor at the school who was convicted on 19 counts including sodomy, assault, and adultery.
Gamble testified that he, Robinson and other drill instructors had engaged in what he called "the game" of sexual relations with recruits, which is prohibited by military law.

The school at Aberdeen has been the site of a major military sexual misconduct scandal that has led to charges against 12 trainers and fuelled a growing controversy over extra-marital sex in the military.
